content.title: About
content.content: Bok choy (Chinese cabbage) is a leafy vegetable from the Brassicaceae family, native to East Asia. Edible parts include crunchy stems and tender leaf blades. Raw bok choy has a mild, slightly sweet flavor and a crisp texture, commonly used in salads, pickles, and as a fresh addition to Asian dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Bok choy is often called “Chinese cabbage” and is one of the most popular vegetables in Chinese cuisine.
Unlike regular cabbage, both the stems and leaves of bok choy are eaten, making it very versatile.
It contains more vitamin K than most other leafy greens.
Bok choy grows quickly: from sowing to harvest can be as short as 30–45 days.
In traditional Chinese medicine, bok choy is considered a tonic that supports digestion.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Bok choy provides a high amount of vitamin C, which supports the immune system and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Source of vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Flavonoids and carotenoids in bok choy help combat free radicals and reduce oxidative stress.

items.title: Low‑calorie source of fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion, promotes satiety, and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Provides minerals
items.content: Bok choy supplies calcium, potassium, and magnesium, which are important for muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: Raw leafy vegetables can be contaminated with gastrointestinal pathogens, so thorough washing before consumption is recommended.

items.title: Interaction with anticoagulants
items.content: High vitamin K content may affect the efficacy of blood‑thinning medications.

items.title: Allergic reactions
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to cruciferous vegetables, experiencing skin rashes or swelling.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Bok choy can be eaten raw in salads, thinly sliced in sandwiches, added to smoothies, or used as a crunchy garnish. Stems can be briefly blanched if a softer texture is desired, but keeping them raw preserves the most nutrients.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store bok choy in the refrigerator in a perforated bag or wrapped in a slightly damp towel. When kept properly, it stays fresh for 5–7 days. Remove any wilted leaves to extend shelf life.
